description: Single-panel TEM bright-field micrograph, labelled "(b)" in a white box at the top-left, of Fe–30Mn–11Al–1.2C (wt%) low-density steel after 30% cold-rolling reduction (Fig. 4 also contains a panel (a) for 10% reduction, not supplied here). A black 500 nm scale bar sits in a white box at the bottom-right; no axis ticks, insets, SAED pattern or Miller indices are printed. The field of view is dominated by a dense, wavy dislocation substructure organised into two sets of intersecting dark bands separated by lighter, relatively dislocation-free channels — the Taylor-lattice / multiple slip-band morphology. Individual dislocations appear as fine dark lines inside the bands, and the intersections of non-coplanar band sets are darkened by heavy dislocation tangles and pile-ups. A large lighter region occupies the centre-right, crossed by fainter parallel bands. The image demonstrates visually that 30% cold rolling produces a well-developed Taylor lattice of multiple interacting slip bands rather than a uniform cell structure. No numbers are visible in the pixels; the reported average slip band spacings (231 nm at 30%, 64 nm at 50% reduction) come only from the text, not from any printed annotation.

subfigures.description: TEM bright-field image of Fe–30Mn–11Al–1.2C steel after 30% cold rolling, 500 nm scale bar bottom-right, showing intersecting dark dislocation slip bands forming a Taylor-lattice structure with lighter dislocation-poor channels and dark tangles at band intersections.

observations.observation: The panel is a TEM bright-field micrograph labelled (b) in a white box at the top-left corner.
A black scale bar labelled '500 nm' is printed inside a white box at the bottom-right of the micrograph.
The microstructure consists of two sets of intersecting dark bands (multiple slip bands) separated by lighter, relatively dislocation-free channels, i.e. a Taylor-lattice morphology.
The intersections of the non-coplanar slip-band sets appear darkest, consistent with locally concentrated dislocation tangles/pile-ups.
No numeric values, no crystallographic indices and no diffraction inset are printed anywhere in this panel.
The caption states this panel is the TEM bright-field image of 30% cold rolling reduction, with panel (a) being 10% reduction (panel (a) is not part of the supplied image).
The citing text states that dislocation pile-ups at the intersections of slip bands are indicated by green arrows in Fig. 4(a); no green arrows are visible in the supplied panel (b).
The citing text states that up to 30% rolled reduction there was no obvious structural variation except a gradual increase of slip bands in Fig. 4(b).
The citing text reports average slip band spacings of 231 nm and 64 nm for 30% and 50% reduction respectively; these values are not printed on the figure.
The citing text interprets the Taylor-lattice structure as the result of planar dislocation glide / 'glide plane softening', with possible cross slip at band intersections.
The caption does not give TEM accelerating voltage, camera length or tilt conditions, so imaging parameters are unknown.

Panel (a) mentioned by the caption (10% reduction) is not present in the supplied image, so no comparison between (a) and (b) can be made from pixels
